identity.paletteIntent: Arena black with poster bone, blood red for kayfabe, ring light gold for labels and steel blue reserved for the real record, so the two channels never blur.
identity.typographyIntent: Heavy slab wood type headlines from old fight posters, condensed card labels and plain sans body text; the real record is set in a newspaper serif italic.
identity.shapeLanguage: Square posters with hard offset shadows, three line ring rope dividers, numbered bouts and stroked chapter numbers.
interactionSignature: headline picker with a reaction time chart
fear filter with a live tally
identity.densityRhythm: Cinematic hero, compact watch prompt, four dense interactive chapters, a paper colored mission break, then a quiet closing question.
identity.archivalBehavior: Library of Congress and Wikimedia Commons photographs are shown uncolored and credited. Video comes only from official channels and loads only on press. No invented archival imagery.
identity.endingLanguage: Return to whether wrestlers were villains or were taught to the crowd as villains, and hand off to the finished exemplar.

assetToInterfaceTranslation.paletteSource: The black arena and hot ring lights of the 1949 Library of Congress frames, plus the red and bone of a printed fight card.
assetToInterfaceTranslation.edgeTreatment: Hard rectangular frames and offset poster shadows; no rounded consumer cards.
assetToInterfaceTranslation.controlLanguage: Headlines look like front pages, filters look like card chips, and the year switcher marks heel red and face steel.
assetToInterfaceTranslation.spacingLanguage: Wide two column story rows alternate with full width instruments and a sticky tally beside the card.
assetToInterfaceTranslation.transitionLanguage: Natural scrolling with short fade reveals; reduced motion shows everything immediately.
